# L02: Sound for AI-made edits (Openverse, Real SFX, earshot)

Unnamed Instagram creator · ig-reel · https://www.instagram.com/p/De9yxpuIG6X/ · notes: [lessons/02_ai-edit-sound-stack.md](../../brain/lessons/02_ai-edit-sound-stack.md)

**Core lesson:** An edit with no SFX feels like a silent movie; a library (Openverse), a placer (Real SFX) and ears (earshot) give AI edits real sound on every visual event.


## Ideas from this source (15)

- **[Question on a pain point](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pain-question)** · hooks: Open with a question about the viewer's pain: "Does your animation look robotic?", "Why do your Claude edits look pro but sound like a silent movie?". Caleb calls a thought-provoking question a "thumbs stopper".
- **[Contrast hook: looks X, sounds Y](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrast-looks-sounds)** · hooks: Two-part contrast on screen: "Looks pro. Sounds like this: 🔇". Sets up the problem in one glance.
- **[State an honest limitation](../topics/story.md#story-honest-limitation)** · story: "The honest part: it only ships 78 sounds." Admitting a limit makes the rest believable.
- **[Something new on screen every 1.2–2.5 s](../topics/editing.md#edit-change-every-1-5-2-5s)** · editing: Change something (cut, layout swap, label, card, animation) every 1.5–2.5 s (L01, L02). Rahul measured at roughly every 1.2–2 s in every reel; his sponsored Flipkart reel was the fastest at 1.2 s.
- **[A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event)** · sound: An edit without SFX feels like a "silent movie": put a pop, click, whoosh or snap on every visual change.
- **[Export silent; pick a low-use track in-app](../topics/sound.md#sound-low-use-count-track)** · sound: Khandala was exported silent and the music chosen in Edits with the use count checked (under ~10K uses is ideal); a place-name song adds nostalgia. Our early edits went out silent this way (L02).
- **[Free SFX from Openverse, CC0 only](../topics/sound.md#sound-openverse-cc0)** · sound: Openverse searches millions of openly licensed sounds with no API key; use CC0 for Instagram; CC-BY needs credit in the caption.
- **[UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui)** · effects: Interface elements and text pops use a spring that overshoots its target a little, then settles (spring/bounce slide-ins in L02; spring UI cards in L07).
- **[Animated number counters](../topics/effects.md#fx-number-counter)** · effects: Numbers count up on screen (5,220,123 sounds, GitHub stars ticking; Rahul's odometer ₹ counter and an opening price ticker counting to ₹75,000).
- **[n/3 progress badges in list videos](../topics/effects.md#fx-progress-badges)** · effects: Numbered 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges mark each item in a list video and hold attention.
- **[Frosted cards, drawn diagrams, red arrows](../topics/effects.md#fx-frosted-glass-cards)** · effects: Frosted-glass UI cards (L01, L02), drawn diagrams (curves, radar, fishing line) and red circles/arrows that guide the eye (L01).
- **[Serif italic emphasis + sans body](../topics/text.md#text-serif-italic-emphasis)** · text: Emphasis words in serif italic (*pro*, *honest*), body in clean sans, keyword highlights in yellow/orange. Our Khandala reel used Instrument Serif Italic.
- **[Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta)** · growth: "Comment 'hooks' and I'll send it to you": a comment-to-DM freebie, with social proof (700K views) raising its value. Rahul uses it on nearly every reel with the keyword in the caption and as a big yellow label in the last 2–4 s.
- **[Show the comment → DM funnel on screen](../topics/growth.md#growth-show-the-funnel)** · growth: The ending shows a mock comment box with the keyword being typed, then a DM preview with the freebie; Rahul's freebies are living resources (live-price part lists, tier list, checklist), not a repeat of the video.
- **[AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement)** · ai-tools: AI editors can't hear. Real SFX places a real recording on each moment, ducks it under voice and outputs MP4 + WAV + report (only 78 UI sounds, so pair it with a library); earshot critiques the mix and sync and makes whooshes in code.
